title: The Man on Floor Forty-Nine
excerpt: Everyone thinks the quiet intern is ordinary—until the company founder calls him by another name.

sections.title: The Intern
paragraphs: Daniel carried coffee, fixed printers, and sat in meetings where no one remembered to ask his opinion.
For eight months, anonymity was the most expensive thing he owned.

sections.title: Floor Forty-Nine
paragraphs: The elevator opened on forty-nine by mistake.
The founder looked up from the conference table and said, 'Mr. Hale, we weren't expecting you until next quarter.'
Behind Daniel, three executives stopped breathing at once.

sections.title: Monday
paragraphs: On Monday he returned to the same desk.
No one asked him to make coffee.
He did anyway, because power, he had learned, was easiest to understand when nobody knew you had it.
